note: From the OpenStreetMap export (OSM's main API, 13 October 2026; tools/osm-to-kit.mjs) and the view from above (docs/reference/aerial/romiley.jpg), 1.25 times real across the line like the tracks: two side platforms on the Marple line, about 103 m long (u -51 to 52), 2.1 m outside its two tracks, platform 1 (the halt's, towards Manchester) on the west side; the B6104 runs under the south half of the platforms on a girder bridge (Stockport Road on the west, Compstall Road on the east, u -47 to -15); a footpath from platform 1 runs behind the station building and down to Stockport Road opposite the Romiley Arms, and one from platform 2 to Station Approach, the lane and car park along the east side; the Romiley Junction signal box (disused) stands behind platform 1's north end, and the junction itself is about 120 m north of the station's point. Trains stop 20 m south of the station's point, so a two-car unit stands on the platforms as they are and a six-car one once they're extended south. Positive v is east. Photos (docs/reference/photos/romiley: platform-1.jpg Gerald England 2025, platform-crossover-1.jpg and entrance-1.jpg DS Pugh 2026, platform-1-east-1.jpg and platform-2-1.jpg JThomas 2019, ramp-1.jpg England 2017, overview-1.jpg Colin Park 2021, signalbox-1.jpg Stephen Craven 2016, area-bridge-1.jpg England 2012): the booking office is a red-brick Victorian building at the back of platform 1, two storeys under gables at its north end and a single-storey range south of it with a canopy on iron columns along its front (with the canopy); platform 2 has a smaller brick building with a canopy at its north end (with the second platform's canopy). There is no footbridge in any photo or in the export: passengers cross by the road under the bridge, so the way across is the ramp down to Stockport Road and the path to Station Approach (the ramp's fall to the street is the terrain's). The bridge's sides are green riveted girders under stone copings. The lifts are the game's (the real station is step-free by its ramps). The car park lies along Station Approach east of the line (from the export's parking aisle and the view from above; its size a guess); the bus stops are the export's (Stop B on Stockport Road for the rail replacement buses, Stop A on Compstall Road for the bus link). No taxi rank in the photos or the export, so none. Lamps, the shelters and the departure boards placed by eye; the cycle stands from memory; the shop is the game's.
